availableCommands.name: cloudflare
availableCommands.description: Comprehensive Cloudflare platform skill covering Workers, Pages, storage (KV, D1, R2), AI (Workers AI, Vectorize, Agents SDK), feature flags (Flagship), networking (Tunnel, Spectrum), security (WAF, DDoS), and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Pulumi). availableCommands.name: cloudflare-email-service
availableCommands.description: Send and receive transactional emails with Cloudflare Email Service (Email Sending + Email Routing). Use when building email sending (Workers binding or REST API), email routing, Agents SDK email handling, or integrating email into any app — Workers, Node.js, Python, Go, etc. Also use for email deliverability, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, wrangler email setup, MCP email tools, or when a coding agent needs to send emails. Even for simple requests like "add email to my Worker" — this skill has critical config details.

availableCommands.name: cloudflare-one
availableCommands.description: Guides Cloudflare One Zero Trust and SASE work across Access, Gateway, WARP, Tunnel, Cloudflare WAN, DLP, CASB, device posture, and identity. availableCommands.name: cloudflare-one-migrations
availableCommands.description: Plans migrations from Zscaler ZIA/ZPA, Palo Alto, legacy VPN, SWG, or SASE stacks to Cloudflare One. Use for migration assessments, policy mapping, rollout plans, and parity/gap analysis.

availableCommands.name: durable-objects
availableCommands.description: Create and review Cloudflare Durable Objects. Use when building stateful coordination (chat rooms, multiplayer games, booking systems), implementing RPC methods, SQLite storage, alarms, WebSockets, or reviewing DO code for best practices. Covers Workers integration, wrangler config, and testing with Vitest. Biases towards retrieval from Cloudflare docs over pre-trained knowledge.

availableCommands.name: run-workflow
availableCommands.description: How to write and run a dynamic workflow script with the `run_workflow` tool: a Python script that orchestrates many agents with `agent`, `parallel`, `pipeline`, and `phase`. Use when a task splits into many independent or staged pieces of agent work (fan out over files, modules, bugs, or review angles, then aggregate), or when the user asks for a workflow. Don't use for a single delegated task (use a subagent) or for legacy workflow files (see migrate-workflows).

availableCommands.name: sandbox-migrate-to-next
availableCommands.description: Use when porting a Cloudflare Sandbox app from stable @cloudflare/sandbox to @cloudflare/sandbox@next (Sandbox SDK 1.0 preview), or when the user asks to migrate or upgrade to Sandbox 1.0 / @next. Not for day-to-day stable work (sandbox-stable) or new @next apps (sandbox-next).

availableCommands.name: sandbox-next
availableCommands.description: Use when building or changing Cloudflare Sandbox apps on @cloudflare/sandbox@next (Sandbox SDK 1.0 preview)—code execution, AI runners, interpreters, CI-like jobs, terminals, files, mounts, tunnels, preview URLs, lifecycle, or errors. Not for the default stable package (use sandbox-stable) or for porting stable to @next (use sandbox-migrate-to-next).

availableCommands.name: sandbox-stable

Not for @cloudflare/sandbox@next (use sandbox-next) or for porting to 1.0 (use sandbox-migrate-to-next).

availableCommands.name: swarm
availableCommands.description: (Preview & Quota Heavy) Run a swarm: several agents working in parallel on one task, each in its own conversation, collaborating through a shared message board. Use when the work splits into pieces that can be done at the same time, or when a second pair of eyes should check the first pair's work.

availableCommands.name: turnstile-spin
availableCommands.description: Set up Cloudflare Turnstile end-to-end in a project. Scan the codebase, create the widget via the Cloudflare API, embed it where user requests need bot verification (form submissions, SPA actions, API endpoints, download links, comment or vote submissions, etc.), wire canonical server-side siteverify in the customer's existing backend, validate, and persist the skill. Load this when a user asks to add Turnstile, set up CAPTCHA, protect a form or endpoint from bots, or fix a Turnstile integration. Mirrors developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/spin.

**Initiating Swarm Process**

I'm initiating the swarm process as requested. I understand the task: a single worker will write "d" to d.txt, then report completion. This simple instruction is the focus of my current operation. I'm preparing to issue the specific command now.

**Analyzing User Instructions**

I'm focused on the user's explicit instructions. Specifically, I'm noting the clear limitations: a single worker, and that the output must be the letter "d" written to "d.txt." My aim is to ensure all actions strictly adhere to this outlined task, avoiding any unnecessary roles or reporting beyond the single requested output and concise completion notification.

**Clarifying Workflow Essentials**

I'm solidifying the core actions. The process simplifies: write "d" to "d.txt", then a brief completion report. Redundant roles are off the table. I'm focusing on the single worker configuration, ensuring the `/swarm` instruction is adhered to. The swarm naming structure is defined, with the worker's brief instructions tailored for the task: write "d" to "d.txt" and then report [done]. I'm considering the workspace implications, realizing a single worker means shared or inherited by default, so it's not a major issue here.

**Confirming Workspace Inheritance**

I've clarified the workspace specifics. Inherited means the worker directly interacts with the coordinator's workspace. Confirmed that means `/workspace` is the current working directory. I'm noting the implications: any file written will be accessible to the coordinator. The Git rules are being evaluated and considered, including working directory implications.

**Evaluating Swarm Interactions**

I'm now shifting focus to the swarm's role and my interactions with it. The recent information highlighted key constraints: I shouldn't be performing technical work; that's the swarm's domain. My role is to oversee, not execute. This reinforces the need to use `run_command` via swarm. I am clarifying how to check the git status within `/workspace`, and the workflow for `post_message` and similar board tools. Specifically I must wait one turn after swarm creation to view board tools, per step 5 in start it. I am focused on responding briefly and efficiently.

**Refining Swarm Commands**

I'm now refining the swarm interaction commands. I realized I can call `swarm` with both `title` and `add` actions in parallel, which is more efficient. I will issue: `swarm{action:"title", title:"d.txtの作成"}` and then `swarm{action:"add", name:"writer", brief:"/workspace/d.txt に「d」と書き込んでください。作業が完了したら @coordinator [done] d.txt に「d」と書き込みました と報告してください。"}`. My focus is streamlined, aiming to trigger the swarm to perform the designated task: writing "d" to "d.txt." I am also checking what model we are running on, as the user settings have changed.

**Confirming Workspace Inheritance**

I am now solidifying the workspace strategy, specifically for this current setup. It's becoming clear that for a single worker, leaving the `workspace` parameter unset is appropriate. This defaults the worker to inheriting the coordinator's workspace, which is exactly what I intend. This reinforces that the worker will operate within `/workspace`, ensuring direct access to the files I need it to manipulate. The implications of this are well understood, based on the previous evaluation of the `native_swarm/SKILL.md` file. I am verifying this against the worker setup, ensuring efficiency.

**Refining Worker Instructions**

I'm now refining the worker instructions. I'm confirming that because the workspace is inherited, the worker will directly write "d" to `d.txt` within the shared directory. I'm verifying that `/workspace` is the correct path. I will check to see if the target repo has git and update the instructions accordingly, adding "Gitリポジトリの場合はコミットも行ってください。" to cover both cases. Finally, I've confirmed that update steps are unnecessary for this simple task.
